producer_report.summary: Added `Urgent` above `High` in plan ordering. A dependency still runs first, and a prerequisite takes the best priority of what needs it. `Priority: urgent` now parses. A new record kind, `athena.priority/1` (`priority-<n>.json`), is appended by `athena priority <job> <level>`. It is accepted only for a queued request and only for urgent, high, normal or low. The request record is not touched. `JobRecords::priority()` resolves one priority for both plan and status: latest priority record, else the request's `Priority:` line, else urgent if the latest reading has an `urgent_reason`, else normal. `ReadingOutput` and `Reading` gained `urgent_reason`. The urgent-marking rule is the field's doc comment in `outputs.rs`, so it appears as the schema description. `reader.md` is unchanged and the budget test is unaffected. The fake reader marks requests that name speed-up words. D122 is appended after D121 only (47 added lines, 0 removed), with a CHANGELOG entry and `docs/records.md` updated. A new test in `decisions.rs` parses the log. It checks every entry has a Provenance bullet and ids ascend. It also pins the first 230046 bytes by SHA-256, taken from the unmodified base file, so only appending passes. This guards the root cause of the earlier D121/D122 damage, which was a mid-file insertion that nothing checked.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: Athena::set_priority is in reading.rs (next to ask/correct/queue), not store.rs; store.rs holds JobRecords.priorities and priority().
reader.md is unchanged; the urgent rule reaches the reader only through the reading schema's field description, not the prompt text.
The log guard pins the base prefix by length and SHA-256, so each later appended entry needs the constants advanced by hand (noted in the test comment and D122's Tradeoff).
The fake reader's trigger words (SPEED_WORDS in fake.rs) are a stand-in for a model's judgment.
When no priority record or text line exists, a reading's urgent_reason makes the job urgent; an explicit 'Priority: normal' line does not block that.
mistakes: My first guard negative tests were wrong (an out-of-order id was caught before the 'changed' check, and a truncation removed the Provenance text); I fixed them before running.
learnings: The Reader set budget test counts only prompt components, not the JSON schema, so a field description in outputs.rs reaches the reader without costing budget.
Queued means no readings and no invocations, so a priority record does not change a job's state.
Unread requests have no acceptance and are refused by the plan gate, so plan-order tests must read them first with drain::plan.
Records::request_jobs() returns a Vec, not an iterator.
athena-cli reaches SHA-256 through athena_data::sha256_hex, so no new dependency or Cargo.lock change was needed.
The base docs/decisions.md was 230046 bytes, ending after D121; prefix SHA-256 bbb3929b73240f6c45520338447ec5b17083aa2a96a171674ac2999b0b5bdca1.
